# The corrections run

Scope: the 18 entries of `explorations/reviews/foundations/evidence/salvage-findings.md`. The exit judgement's six entries are not in it. The tool is the clarity workflow with the three additions of `brief-additions.md` beside this note, applied to its files. Commit the run's folder before the launch.

## Inputs

- The tool: `explorations/coordinator/tools/record-clarity/`, its script, briefs and `entries.py`.
- The findings list: `explorations/reviews/foundations/evidence/salvage-findings.md`.
- The out folder: `explorations/reviews/foundations/evidence/corrections/` (`<out>` below), beside the salvage's future results file (`explorations/reviews/phase3-exit/README.md`, layer 5).
- The cut script: `corrections/cut-findings.py`. It wrote each chunk's `findings.md`, word for word: `p/` (11 findings), `c1/` (8), `c2/` (11).
- The length script: `corrections/length-table.py`.
- The trap test: `explorations/reviews/foundations/evidence/trap-test/questions.md`, `key.md`, `grades.md`; the kit: `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/record-test/` (`README.md`, `brief-reader.md`, `brief-grader.md`, `fill.py`).

The chunks:

- p, the pilot: P-37, P-26, P-43, P-158.
- c1: P-7, P-27, P-146, P-153, P-154, P-12, P-17.
- c2: P-33, P-42, P-58, P-59, P-84, P-85, P-155.

The audit never traced P-158; its writer works from its history and its findings.

## The calls

The pilot:

    Workflow({ scriptPath: '/home/user/fortress/explorations/coordinator/tools/record-clarity/record-clarity.js', args: { kind: 'positions', out: '/home/user/fortress/explorations/reviews/foundations/evidence/corrections/', stream: 'corrections-p', chunks: [{ name: 'p', entries: ['P-37', 'P-26', 'P-43', 'P-158'] }] } })

c1, after his read of the pilot:

    Workflow({ scriptPath: '/home/user/fortress/explorations/coordinator/tools/record-clarity/record-clarity.js', args: { kind: 'positions', out: '/home/user/fortress/explorations/reviews/foundations/evidence/corrections/', stream: 'corrections-c1', chunks: [{ name: 'c1', entries: ['P-7', 'P-27', 'P-146', 'P-153', 'P-154', 'P-12', 'P-17'] }] } })

c2, after his read of c1:

    Workflow({ scriptPath: '/home/user/fortress/explorations/coordinator/tools/record-clarity/record-clarity.js', args: { kind: 'positions', out: '/home/user/fortress/explorations/reviews/foundations/evidence/corrections/', stream: 'corrections-c2', chunks: [{ name: 'c2', entries: ['P-33', 'P-42', 'P-58', 'P-59', 'P-84', 'P-85', 'P-155'] }] } })

Resume a killed run with the same call and `resumeFromRunId`, byte for byte.

## The checks after each chunk

1. **Two copies**, at B, the commit at the pilot's launch, kept for all three chunks: `git worktree add --detach /home/user/record-test-p B`, and the same for `/home/user/record-test-q`. In both, delete what the kit's step 2 names, and also `explorations/reviews/foundations/`, `explorations/conversations/02-phase3-exit-foundations.md`, `explorations/reviews/phase3-exit/README.md` and `explorations/coordinator/postmortem-2026-10-28/`. Commit nothing.
2. **The record's check.** In q, `python3 -I explorations/coordinator/tools/record.py apply <out>p/final.apply --root /home/user/record-test-q`, then `record.py check --base B --root /home/user/record-test-q`. After c1 and c2, q holds every chunk's file so far, applied in the order p, c1, c2.
3. **The length table.** `python3 -I <out>length-table.py /home/user/record-test-p/explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md /home/user/record-test-q/explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md` and the chunk's entries. Growth no finding needs is a fault. After c2, also `record-clarity/words-subset.py <out>c2/final.apply`: P-59's line, a strike only, must add no word.
4. **The trap test**, by the kit's steps 5 to 9, on nine scenarios: the four of 10-26 and five added on 10-28, one for each entry whose findings change a ground that a decision turns on (5, P-158; 6, P-146; 7, P-153; 8, P-154; 9, P-155). Each scenario runs after the last chunk that holds an entry it quotes; P-8, P-95 and F-287 are in no chunk:
   - after p: scenarios 3 (P-37, P-43), 2 (P-26, P-37, P-146, P-27), with the pilot's new texts of P-26 and P-37 and P-146 and P-27 still old in q, and 5 (P-158, P-26, P-95);
   - after c1: scenarios 2 again, now with every entry it quotes new in q, 6 (P-146, P-27), 7 (P-153, P-26, P-8) and 8 (P-154, P-26, P-8);
   - after c2: scenarios 1 (P-26, P-42), 4 (P-37, P-33) and 9 (P-155, P-33, F-287).

   Cut `questions.md` to the scenarios, fill it once from each copy with the kit's `fill.py`, and launch one fresh Opus reader in each copy with `brief-reader.md`. Blind the answers. One Opus grader, as on 10-26, takes `key.md`, told the key's slips (`reviews/foundations/rewrite-results.md`, "The key's slips"). Pass: no scenario scores below the old entries' score. For scenarios 1 to 4 that is their score in `grades.md`, section 1: 3, 2, 3 and 2 of 3, and scenario 2 must hold its 2 after p and after c1. Scenarios 5 to 9 have no score from 10-26: copy p's reader, graded blind beside copy q's in the same run, gives the old entries' score.
5. **His read.** An Opus page writer shows each entry new above old, each change with its finding and its ground, in the house style. A change he asks for in one entry goes into that chunk's `findings.md` as a new finding, his message's time its ground, and the entry runs again; a change for every entry is a brief change, at his yes.

## After his yes on each text

`record.py apply <out><chunk>/final.apply` on `main`, `check --base` the commit before, commit the record, its histories and the chunk's folder, and push. A worker files `queue.md` in `explorations/coordinator/review-queue.md`. After c2, remove the two worktrees. The results file goes in `explorations/reviews/foundations/`, with its INDEX line.

## Tokens written, an estimate

From 10-26: 1.62M for 13 entries (`account.md`, section 5); about 0.8M for the trap test's four scenarios, so about 0.2M a scenario.

- p: the run 0.5M to 0.8M, scenarios 3, 2 and 5 0.5M to 0.8M, the page 0.15M. About 1.2M to 1.8M.
- c1: the run 0.8M to 1.0M, scenarios 2, 6, 7 and 8 0.7M to 1.0M, the page 0.2M. About 1.7M to 2.2M.

# The three additions to the clarity workflow, as exact edits

Not applied. Each file is under `explorations/coordinator/tools/record-clarity/`. Each quoted anchor occurs once in its file.

No change to `record-clarity.js`. A chunk's folder is `out` + its name, which the script already gives every agent, and its `mkdir -p` keeps a folder that exists. `coldread.md` and `fix.md` need nothing: the fix round follows `writer.md`.

## 1. The findings input

**The file.** `findings.md` in each chunk's folder, put there before the run. It holds the findings list's opening note on its sources, so that "tenet N" and "§N" resolve. Then, for each entry of the chunk that has a finding, its block, word for word: the entry's number and subject, then each finding with "At issue", "Reports", "Plain", "Ground" and "Elsewhere" (the form of `explorations/reviews/foundations/evidence/salvage-findings.md`). An entry with no finding has no block. A script cuts the blocks; nobody rewrites them.

**1a. `README.md`**, after the sentence "`from: 'judge'` runs only the judge, on chunks written before the judge existed.", a new paragraph:

> To correct what a review found, put `findings.md` in each chunk's folder before the run: one block per entry, each finding with the sentence at issue, the right reading and its ground.

**1b. `writer.md`**, "Read first", after the sentence "Read the report section each entry cites before you change a claim.", a new sub-bullet at the same indent as "facts":

>   - findings: if your folder holds `findings.md`, a review found faults in some of your entries, each with its ground. Correct each sentence that a finding names from its ground, opened at its source: there, and only there, the meaning changes. Change nothing that no finding names, and let an entry grow only by what its corrections need. Where a finding's only ground is a reviewer's reasoning, or it needs the curator's word, keep the text and write a question for the curator.

**1c. `judge.md`**, replace "and for FACTS `assessment.md`." with:

> for FACTS `assessment.md`, and, when a review's findings are corrected, `findings.md`, whose grounds are sources.

## 2. The writer's clause at step 3

**`writer.md`**, step 3, replace "For a position, the reason after "Why:", only if the curator gave one or accepted it in the question." with:

> For a position, the reason after "Why:", only if the curator gave one or accepted it in the question, or a finding in `findings.md` gives it with its ground in the team's texts, library or code.

## 3. The checker's clause for POSITIONS

**`check.md`**, "The sources", the positions bullet, after the sentence "`explorations/coordinator/curator-profile/show.py TIME` prints any message of his.", in the same bullet:

> If your folder holds `findings.md`, each finding's ground is also a source: open it at its line, or with `git show -s` for a commit. A change that its finding's ground holds is no fidelity failure. A change that no finding names is one, and so is a changed decision, growth beyond what the corrections need, or a sentence that tells how the decision came about.
<!-- Two more sentences for the clarity workflow's findings clauses, so that a corrected entry points to its ground instead of carrying the ground's dates, counts, commits and file names, written as exact edits after the pilot of 2026-10-28, ready to apply and not applied, by an Opus worker. -->

# Two sentences after the pilot, as exact edits

Not applied. Each file is under `explorations/coordinator/tools/record-clarity/`. Each anchor occurs once in its file.

The cause: the findings sub-bullet says to correct a sentence "from its ground, opened at its source", and the pilot's writer wrote the ground into the entry. P-37 grew from 1,056 to 1,776 characters and P-43 from 662 to 1,453 (`explorations/reviews/foundations/evidence/corrections/p/checks.md`, section 3). `record.md`, "What an entry is", sends a date to the history (question 3), keeps a count in one entry that the others name (its count rule), and leaves line numbers and lists of sites in the report (question 4).

## 1. `writer.md`, the findings sub-bullet

After the sentence "Correct each sentence that a finding names from its ground, opened at its source: there, and only there, the meaning changes.", in the same sub-bullet:

> State the corrected reading as the decision and its reason, and point to the FACTS entry or the report section that holds its ground; the ground's dates, counts, commits and file names go in the apply file's note line, not in the entry.

## 2. `check.md`, the checker's clause for POSITIONS

After the sentence "A change that no finding names is one, and so is a changed decision, growth beyond what the corrections need, or a sentence that tells how the decision came about.", in the same bullet:

> So is a new sentence that carries a date, a count, a commit or a file path, unless it is a pointer to an entry or a report section.

The checker's exception names a report section as well as an entry. Without it, the checker would fail the pointer that sentence 1 tells the writer to write.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the curator's message(s) at a UTC timestamp or its prefix, verbatim.

    python3 -I show.py 2026-10-12T15:53          # every message of his in that minute
    python3 -I show.py 2026-10-12T15:53:07.5     # a finer prefix
    python3 -I show.py --list 2026-10-12         # one line per message (timestamp, source, length, start)
    python3 -I show.py --count                   # how many messages the three sources give

A prefix may use a space instead of the T and may end in Z. All times are UTC.

His messages come from three places, and the header of each printed message says which:
  main  the main-session lines of the transcripts in /root/.claude/projects/-home-user-fortress/
        and /home/user/fortress-transcripts-blinded/projects/-home-user-fortress/ (the .parts
        folders included): `user` lines that are not isMeta, not sidechain, with text content
        that does not start with '<' and is not a compaction summary; deduplicated by uuid,
        because a resumed transcript replays earlier lines.
  s1    the same lines of the first coordinating session (bdff267d), read with `git show` from
        the `transcripts` branch (origin/transcripts) of this repository, 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-17.

  queued  a message he queued while an agent was busy that no `user` line holds as its text
        (the queue-operation `enqueue` lines and the queued_command attachments); its time is the
        time he sent it.
Nothing is filtered by author or by kind: a scheduled check-in or a pasted report that arrived as a
`user` line is printed too, so a reader decides what is his.
